result: In 34 PCC vs 36 recovered controls, controls improved more than PCC on repeated processing-speed tests (coding; Color-Word speed composite p=.031, partial eta2=.08), indicating cognitive performance fatigability, with no correlation between performance fatigability, perceived fatigability and trait fatigue.
reason: Measures cognitive (processing-speed) fatigability in long COVID, not motor grip fatigability or motor-network fMRI; fits the processing-speed deficit finding as a long COVID, within-session extension.

result: Exploratory factor analysis of self-reported neurocognitive items in 2,313 ME/CFS and 299 PASC patients found two factors in each group: classic memory/concentration symptoms and a separate sensory overload (noise/light hypersensitivity) factor.
reason: Large self-report sample showing sensory hypersensitivity forms a distinct symptom domain in ME/CFS and PASC; extends the self-reported sensitivity claim; no prevalence or controls.

result: Exploratory factor analysis of self-reported neurocognitive items in 2,313 ME/CFS and 299 PASC patients found two factors: memory/concentration symptoms and sensory overload.
reason: Self-report symptom factor structure with no objective testing or controls; does not test the meta-analytic performance deficits claimed; covered by the neuro-sensory link.

result: In 28 post-COVID patients with persistent subjective cognitive decline after mild COVID, voxelwise FDG-PET showed hypometabolism in bilateral frontal, temporal and parietal lobes and left occipital lobe versus healthy controls.
reason: Same measure (FDG-PET hypometabolism in long COVID), adds a positive series with frontal hypometabolism to the contested finding; small sample, cognitively selected.

result: The same 28 post-COVID patients showed predominantly frontal EEG slowing versus age- and sex-matched controls, with increased relative delta and theta power and reduced alpha power in frontal, temporal and central regions.
reason: Quantitative EEG spectral power differences in long COVID versus controls, the same measure the finding covers (ME/CFS and LC); small single-centre sample.

result: In 156 sample/symptom pairs from 79 people 1-6 months after COVID, GI symptoms, chest pain, PEM, smell/taste change, fatigue, brain fog, abnormal movement and palpitations were accompanied by higher IL-10, VEGF, MIP-1a, IL-1b, IL-6, IL-8, MIG, granzyme A and CX3CL1, while cough, dizziness, dyspnea and hair loss were not.
reason: Within-cohort symptom-cytokine associations; does not measure T-cell exhaustion, myeloid shifts, non-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies or cortisol, and the atlas has no long COVID plasma cytokine finding to retarget to.

result: In 79 post-COVID participants, several PASC symptoms (including PEM, fatigue, brain fog) were accompanied by higher IL-10, VEGF, MIP-1a, IL-1b, IL-6, IL-8, MIG, granzyme A and CX3CL1.
reason: The finding is an ME/CFS case-control meta-analysis of TNF, IL-2, IL-4, TGF-beta and CRP; this is a long COVID symptom-stratified comparison of different cytokines with no ME/CFS or uninfected controls.

result: EBV reactivation by PCR (BamHI/LMP2) was found in 40/140 (28.6%) post-COVID patients with persistent fatigue/PEM vs 9/80 (11.3%) matched recovered controls (p=0.003), with higher EBNA-1 IgG (p=0.004) and EA-D IgG (p=0.008).
reason: Independent Egyptian cohort with the same EA-D IgG serology in the same direction; it also reports EBV DNA, which Peluso did not find associated, so it partly goes beyond the finding.

result: In 100 PCS patients vs 50 controls, NIRS during light stress-ball exercise showed decreased deoxygenation peaks at exercise onset in PCS (p=0.0002), and multivariate analysis identified a subgroup in which strong fatigue was associated with restricted oxygenation dynamics.
reason: NIRS muscle oxygenation deficit in long COVID, the same method the finding names; it adds a fatigue-linked subgroup, which bears on the claim that the deficit does not consistently track fatigue.

result: In 100 PCS patients vs 50 controls, local NIRS during light handgrip exercise showed decreased deoxygenation peaks at exercise onset (p=0.0002).
reason: Local forearm NIRS during light exercise is not invasive CPET systemic oxygen extraction or cardiac filling; already covered by the lc-muscle-oxidative-capacity link.
